messages:

Subject: Vendor onboarding: marketplace accounts + PO path

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the intro earlier this week. We’re ready to start the marketplace activation for StratusLy (AWS/Azure/GCP) and I wanted to confirm the procurement path for our finance team. Specifically:

- Which billing entity should our invoices reference for each marketplace (AWS vs Azure vs GCP)?
- Do we need an initial PO from Redwood for marketplace listing, or will invoices be paid against a consolidated monthly invoice?
- Any required vendor intake forms or attestations we should return up-front (tax forms, proof of SOC2, data processing addenda)?

I attached our small vendor intake packet and a draft tax matrix. Can someone outline the steps and a rough timeline for vendor account provisioning and PO creation? We have a product launch target at the end of July and would like to avoid billing/reg delay.

Thanks,
Marcos Silva
Head of Finance & Ops
StratusLy

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding: marketplace accounts + PO path

Hi Marcos,

Great — welcome. Below is the pragmatic onboarding flow we use for marketplace sellers; I’ve kept it tight for finance teams. High-level timeline: 2–3 weeks for documentation + marketplace registration, 1–2 weeks for PO/invoicing alignment in parallel.

1) Vendor intake packet (you already sent the draft) – we’ll use that to seed the seller record.
2) Legal & tax forms – we need: W-9 or W-8 (US/Non-US), EU VAT registration if you invoice Redwood EU entities, and the signed MSA for marketplace transaction pass-throughs (DocuSign link below).
3) Evidence binder – SOC 2 Type II report or letter of attestation; if you don’t have SOC we accept a security questionnaire + compensating controls doc.
4) PO vs invoice model: For AWS Marketplace the listing is typically transacted through AWS and billed on AWS invoices; Redwood requires a PO only when we’re purchasing off-platform (reserved capacity/dedicated). For Azure/GCP marketplace listings, the vendor can either invoice Redwood directly or route via the marketplace depending on partner program. If your finance prefers POs, provide the invoicing entity for each marketplace and we’ll create a purchase order for direct invoicing lanes.

Immediate asks from our side: please confirm the legal invoicing entity(ies) and country for StratusLy, and send the signed intake form + tax matrix. I’ve attached our internal procurement checklist for vendor activation.

DocuSign MSA: https://docusign.com/xyz/embedded?doc=MSA-8792
HubSpot deal (internal): https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8792

Next actions:
- Marcos: confirm invoicing entities + return signed intake form (we’ll generate a PO if needed).
- Vanessa: I’m looping you for PO creation and payment terms.
- Laura: please confirm onboarding evidence requirements for marketplace listing ops.

Thanks — Mateo
Senior Seller Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_procurement_checklist_v1.2.pdf (stub)

Hi Mateo — thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Invoicing entities: StratusLy, Inc. (US) for AWS and GCP; StratusLy EU LTD for Azure (we have VAT registration).
- We prefer PO-backed invoices for any direct billing lanes (Net 30). For marketplace-hosted transactions we expect the platform to handle billing.

We’ll sign the intake form and return it today. Two quick questions: if we surface compensating controls instead of SOC2, what level of evidence do you need? Also, does Redwood require a specific invoice header or PO number format for automated ingestion?

Best,
Marcos

Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding: marketplace accounts + PO path

Hi Marcos — looping in procurement ops details.

Short answers:
- Evidence with compensating controls: acceptable if you provide (1) a completed security questionnaire, (2) 3rd-party vulnerability scan summary, and (3) a written compensating controls matrix. We’ll do a light risk review and put any exceptions in an evidence memo.
- Invoice header / PO format: Our AP system expects: Invoice header (Vendor legal name), Invoice number, Invoice date, PO number (if applicable), Line item description (SKU), Unit price, Tax amount, Total. PO numbers are 8 digits, prefix 40 (e.g., 40123456). If you send invoices to invoices@redwood.com and include the PO number as the subject, our AP auto-ingest will pick them up.

Procurement timeline & payment terms: For PO-backed lanes we typically do Net 30 from invoice receipt after acceptance. For marketplace-hosted transactions (AWS listing) the payment cadence is governed by the platform. If you want a PO for Azure direct invoicing we can provision that once we receive the signed intake, W-9/VAT proof, and evidence binder.

I’ll create the PO record once Mateo confirms the invoicing entity mapping in our system. If you want priority processing for your July launch, please mark the HubSpot deal as "Launch Priority" and reply-all with a clear list of documents you’ll upload to the Drive link.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
